localChanges: Pillaging a square now takes its improvement's yields away straight away, where the square used to go on producing as if it were still there (closes #413).
A city that has sold an improvement can't sell another that turn even after the game is saved and loaded again (closes #679).
Whether a city can buy a unit now follows the civil disorder its screen shows: while it shows disorder you can't, even after rearranging its citizens, as in Civ1 (closes #680).
A city you rename keeps its name to itself: no city founded later is given the same one (closes #712).

log: Pillage.complete unregistered the improvement itself, so the Pillaged rules never ran: the square's yield cache wasn't cleared and tile-improvement:pillaged never fired, and a pillaged square kept its old improvement's yields (civ-clone/web-renderer#413). It now processes Pillaged for the improvement and leaves the removal to the ruleset, as building one goes through Built. A tile with nothing on it is left alone.
Adds the package's first tests and CI that installs with pnpm, checks prettier and the committed JavaScript, and runs them; drops package-lock.json (civ-clone/web-renderer#66).

Built and Removed improvements cleared each player's cached yields for the square, but Pillaged did not, so once pillaging goes through its rules a player's view of the square could still show the old improvement's yields (civ-clone/web-renderer#413). Pillaged now does the same.
A city's last sale is now kept as a civ1-treasury:sold pending effect, which saves carry, so loading mid-turn no longer allows a second sale (civ-clone/web-renderer#679).
A unit can be bought in civil disorder only by the disorder recorded when the turn was processed, as v474.05 checks the city's recorded status (civ-clone/web-renderer#680).

claim(name) takes every copy of a name out of the pools, whatever its case, and a City #n fallback skips claimed numbers, so a renamed city's name isn't handed out again, also after a save and load (civ-clone/web-renderer#712).
CI now checks the committed JavaScript matches the source, and package-lock.json is dropped (civ-clone/web-renderer#66).
